data.title: The docs migration excludes probe-b-candidates.md, and the journal is checked for people before it is pushed
data.why: The migration put all 66 documents into the journal, and the journal is committed to a public repository. One of them names ten real people by their GitHub handle, with what they said in public and why they would be worth interviewing. The file says so about itself - names real people who never asked to be in it, decide whether it belongs in git at all - and strategy.md already carried it as an open item, probe-b-candidates.md out of git before the next push. The migration would have made that push. Caught before any commit, so the fix was to delete sixty-six untracked events and run the migration again with the file excluded: the script is deterministic, so the labels and the 389 rewritten links came back consistent. Removing only that one document would have shifted every DOC-N after it and pointed 400 links at the wrong documents - the I7 risk that comes with linking by a derived label.
data.rejected: Deleting only that document's event: labels are assigned by ULID order, so every document after it shifts and every link past it breaks.; Publishing it and redacting later: the journal is append-only and git is a clone, so a later revision does not unpublish what a mirror already fetched.
